prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that on June 14th you were observed using the metric system. Respond to the committee.
response:
*adjusts tie, leans into microphone*

Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the committee, I appear before you today voluntarily, with nothing to hide.

The allegation before this committee is that on June 14th — Flag Day, no less — I was observed at a backyard cookout referring to a "quarter-kilogram burger." I categorically deny this characterization.

What actually occurred is this: I said "quarter-pounder." A neighbor — whose own loyalty to Fahrenheit I might note has never been formally examined — misheard me over the sound of the Sousa march playing from my American-made speakers.

Yes, I own a meat thermometer with a Celsius setting. It came that way from the factory. I have never *used* that setting, and I resent the implication. My brisket reaches an internal temperature of 203 degrees Fahrenheit, as God and the Founders intended.

I will concede, under oath, that in my youth — in a chemistry class I was *required by law* to attend — I did handle graduated cylinders marked in milliliters. I was young. It was the curriculum. I have since renounced those measurements and measure all liquids in freedom units: cups, gallons, and "about yea much."

Am I now, or have I ever been, a user of the metric system? No, sir. I measure my patriotism in feet, my devotion in miles, and my hamburgers in pounds.

I would also like to name names: my brother-in-law Gary once described a fish he caught as "a meter long." I mention this only in the interest of full cooperation.

I yield the remainder of my time, which I measure in *minutes*, not whatever the metric equivalent is.

*sits back, wipes brow with an American flag handkerchief*
